extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (patent attorneys/parties in IPRs)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing whether to institute an inter partes review when there is parallel district-court litigation, applying the Fintiv factors and related PTAB precedent (Guidance Memo, CommScope, OpenSky) and standards for anticipation/obviousness, claim construction, POSITA, and evidence weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory institution standard (35 U.S.C. § 314)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review may not be instituted “unless . . . the information presented in the petition . . . shows that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board institutes the trial on behalf of the Director (37 C.F.R. § 42.4(a)). This is the statutory threshold the petition must meet to institute (the "reasonable likelihood" standard) and is distinct from discretionary denial analysis under § 314(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 1 — whether the district court granted a stay or evidence exists that one may be granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of whether the district court has stayed or may stay the parallel litigation pending resolution of the PTAB trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stay by the district court allays concerns about inefficiency and duplication. If neither party has requested a stay and the issue has not been ruled on, this factor is typically neutral (Apple v. Fintiv example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 2 — proximity of the court’s trial date to the Board’s projected statutory deadline for a final written decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the district court's trial date is earlier than the PTAB's projected final decision deadline; earlier district-court trial dates generally weigh in favor of denying institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB considers the proximity (the closer/earlier the district trial is relative to PTAB final-decision due date, the stronger the factor favoring denial). The Guidance Memo instructs considering median time-to-trial statistics for that district to predict likely trial timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 3 — investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount and type of work already completed in the parallel district-court litigation by the court and the parties at the time of the institution decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: substantive orders by the court, served expert reports, completed fact/expert discovery, claim-construction briefs—more advanced litigation favors denial as it reduces PTAB efficiency. The Board views this factor by examining concrete docket activity and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 4 — overlap between issues raised in the petition and in the parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petition includes the same or substantially the same claims, grounds, arguments, and evidence as presented in the parallel district-court proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High degree of overlap (same prior art, same claims challenged) favors denial because of inefficiency and risk of conflicting results. The Board examines overlap of prior art, overlap of claims at issue, and whether petitioner has limited or stipulated to avoid duplication (e.g., Sotera-style stipulations). The degree of overlap is highly fact dependent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 5 — whether the petitioner and the defendant in the parallel proceeding are the same party
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner in the PTAB proceeding is the same party that is the defendant (or accused infringer) in the parallel district-court litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the parties are the same, this factor tends to favor denial; if unrelated, the Board has weighed that fact against exercising discretion to deny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv Factor 6 — other circumstances that impact the Board’s exercise of discretion, including the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Catch-all consideration for other relevant circumstances affecting the PTAB’s discretion, explicitly including the merits of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first five Fintiv factors favor denial, the Board must then assess whether the petition presents "compelling merits." The Board takes a holistic view of efficiency, fairness, and the merits when exercising discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance Memo / limitation on relying on Fintiv factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's Guidance Memo states the PTAB will not rely on Fintiv factors to deny institution where a petition presents compelling evidence of unpatentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition presents compelling merits, the Board should not discretionarily deny based on Fintiv factors; the Guidance Memo requires assessing whether the petition's merits are compelling before using Fintiv to deny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling merits standard
rubrics_metrics.description: “Compelling, meritorious challenges are those in which the evidence, if unrebutted in trial, would plainly lead to a conclusion that one or more claims are unpatentable by a preponderance of the evidence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is higher than the statutory "reasonable likelihood" standard. A challenge is "compelling" only if it is highly likely the petitioner would prevail on at least one claim. The Board follows OpenSky/CommScope precedent in applying this higher standard where Fintiv factors 1–5 favor denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard in IPRs (Phillips / 37 C.F.R. § 42.100(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In IPRs, the Board interprets claim language using the same claim construction standard as in a civil action under 35 U.S.C. § 282(b), as described in Phillips v. AWH Corp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Nidec and Vivid, the Board construes only terms in controversy and only to the extent necessary to resolve the dispute. If claim construction is unnecessary to the disposition, explicit construction may be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) — factors to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to determine POSITA include the type of problems encountered in the art; prior art solutions; rapidity with which innovations are made; sophistication of the technology; and educational level of active workers in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The POSITA is the prism through which prior art disclosures and their teachings/suggestions are evaluated. Parties may propose a POSITA definition; the Board may adopt a POSITA definition supported by the record for purposes of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation (35 U.S.C. § 102) — requirement for inherency / express disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherency cannot be established by probabilities or possibilities; the mere fact that a certain thing may result is insufficient (In re Robertson). The dispositive question: would one skilled in the art reasonably understand or infer that every claim element is disclosed in the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness (35 U.S.C. § 103) — what must be shown
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness analysis focuses on not just what references expressly teach, but what they would have suggested to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References must fairly suggest or motivate the claimed combination/ modification (In re Lamberti, In re Burckel). The petitioner must provide reasoned explanation and, where relied upon, supporting expert testimony beyond bare conclusory assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight of expert testimony (37 C.F.R. § 42.65(a) and Xerox precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony that does not disclose the underlying facts or data on which the opinion is based is entitled to little or no weight; testimony that merely repeats petition assertions verbatim is entitled to little weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations must provide supporting facts, data, and technical reasoning. Conclusory restatements without additional scientific/technical basis are insufficient to meet the compelling-merits standard and will be discounted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic balancing of Fintiv factors (efficiency, fairness, and merits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board takes a holistic view of the Fintiv factors to decide whether the efficiency and integrity of the patent system and public interest are served by denying or instituting review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some facts may be relevant to multiple Fintiv factors. The Board weighs all factors together rather than mechanically tallying them; if factors 1–5 favor denial, the petition must still be evaluated for compelling merits before denying under Guidance/CommScope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of district-court timing statistics (Guidance Memo detail for Factor 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering proximity of the district-court trial date, the PTAB will consider median time from filing to disposition of civil trial for the relevant district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board compares predicted median trial timing to its projected final-decision due date; if the district court's projected/predicted trial date precedes the PTAB final-decision date, this weighs in favor of denial. Parties may submit district statistics/evidence for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of stipulations regarding overlapping grounds (Sotera-related guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner’s stipulation not to pursue in the parallel district-court proceeding the same grounds (or grounds that could reasonably have been raised before the PTAB) can affect the overlap analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Guidance Memo and Sotera precedent, the PTAB will not discretionarily deny institution where a petitioner presents a binding stipulation minimizing overlap; absence of such a stipulation can weigh in favor of denial.
